newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus gets $3.9 billion in new orders.
newsitem.headline: Airbus gets $3.9 billion in new orders.

text.p: Airbus Industrie, the European consortium, landed two big aircraft orders worth $3.9 billion Friday -- a $2.5 billion deal with Virgin Atlantic Airways and a $1.4 billion pact with Air Canada.

Both airlines ordered the new Airbus A340-600 widebody jet, which the consortium just launched at the Paris Airshow in June. The aircraft are aimed at attacking Boeing Co.'s lucrative monopoly at the high-capacity segment with its 777 twinjet and the 747 jumbo jet.
"Getting a launch customer only 1-1/2 months after the commercial launch confirms the need for such a plane," an Airbus spokeswoman said.
Air Canada said it signed a letter of intent to acquire five twin-engine A330-300 aircraft and three four-engine A340-300 aircraft, with options for 20 additional aircraft.
The Canadian flag carrier said it will become the first scheduled airline in North America to operate the A330-300 when it takes delivery of the first aircraft in October 1999.
The value of the eight aircraft, based on list prices, is about $1.4 billion, Air Canada said.
Air Canada said the new aircraft will replace its fleet of six Boeing 747-100/200 aircraft and two A340 aircraft currently under operating leases.
"With one of the youngest and most efficient fleets in the world, Air Canada will be positioned to improve further its operating performance," President Lamar Durrett said in a statement.
The new jets will lower Air Canada's operating costs by at least about $17 million a year once the aircraft are all in service, the airline said.
Virgin said it will acquire 16 Airbus A340-600s and will take delivery of the new aircraft from 2002.

The new planes will have private bedrooms with double beds for premium fare customers. These will be located in the forward lower deck. A bar and lounge area, showers, and exercise and massage area will be located in the aircraft's rear lower deck.
In adddition to the 375-seat version of the four-engine long-haul A340-600 aircraft, Virgin said it was also ordering two more A340-300 jets for delivery next year.
Airbus launched the marketing campaign for the A340-500 and A340-600 at the Paris Le Bourget air show in June.
Managing Director Jean Pierson said at the time that the new plane cost $2.5 billion to develop.
The catalogue price for the A340-500 is $144 million and $158 million for the A340-600, a spokeswoman said.

The A340-600 will carry 378 passengers in three classes and have a range of 7,300 miles. It will have a larger wing for increased lift and fuel capacity and have 20 extra fuselage frames to extend the body.
The A340-500 will carry 313 passengers in three classes and have a range of 8,300 miles.
Both planes will be powered by new engines developed by Britain's Rolls-Royce Plc based on its Trent 500.
The A340-600 is due to enter service in autumn 2001.

Current versions of the A340-200 and A340-300 seat 261 and 295 passengers, respectively, and fly up to 7,200 miles and 7,300 miles, respectively. There is also an A340-8000, a version of the A340-200, which flies up to 8,000 miles.
Airbus is a consortium comprising French state-owned Aerospatiale , British Aerospace Plc , Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA of Spain.
